faqs.question: How much does injector testing cost?
faqs.answer: Pricing depends on injector style. Mechanical injector testing starts at $16, common rail testing starts at $65, HEUI testing ranges from $55 to $85, EUI testing starts at $78, pumpeduse testing is $125, and gasoline injector testing and cleaning starts at $39.

faqs.question: What is the turnaround time?
faqs.answer: Most listed diesel and gasoline injector testing services are quoted at 48 hours. EUI, Cummins STC, and pumpeduse testing are listed at 72 hours. Current workload can affect timing, so contact us for current queue estimates.

faqs.question: What information should I provide when scheduling injectors?
faqs.answer: Provide your name, company if applicable, email, phone number, engine or vehicle application, the complaint or reason for testing, whether the injectors will arrive by drop off or courier, and the expected date of arrival.

faqs.question: Do you provide results after injector testing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Results and recommendations are provided after testing. Common rail testing may include a PDF printout from the Bosch EPS205 computerized test bench where applicable.

faqs.question: Can you test gasoline injectors too?

shortDescription: Bosch common rail injector testing, repair, and calibration on the EPS205 test bench for Duramax, Cummins, Powerstroke, and modern diesel engines.
description: Common rail injectors are more complex than older mechanical diesel injectors and require a different testing process. NW Fuel Injection Services uses the Bosch EPS205 computerized test bench to operate common rail injectors in conditions that closely match real world diesel operation, then measures leak rates, start behavior, idle quantity, pilot injection, emissions quantity, full load quantity, and actuator resistance.

The Bosch EPS205 lets our technicians evaluate each injector under controlled high pressure conditions before repair decisions are made.

featureCards.title: Leak Testing
featureCards.text: High pressure nozzle and control valve leak testing help identify injectors that can cause hard starting, fuel dilution, smoke, rough running, or rail pressure faults.

featureCards.title: Quantity Testing
featureCards.text: Full load quantity, idle quantity, pilot injection quantity, and emissions quantity are measured to confirm how the injector delivers fuel at key operating points.

featureCards.title: Electrical Checks
featureCards.text: Electric buzz testing and actuator resistance checks help reveal electrical faults that can affect injector response and drivability.

featureCards.title: Smarter Replacement
featureCards.text: Testing separates failed injectors from healthy injectors, which can save money compared with replacing every injector without measured results.

faqs.question: Which common rail engines do you service?
faqs.answer: We test common rail injectors for GMC and Chevrolet Duramax engines since 2001, Dodge and Ram Cummins engines since 2003, Ford 6.7 Powerstroke engines since 2011, plus many Cummins industrial, Volvo, Deutz, Volvo Penta, Mack, Volkswagen, BMW, and Mercedes applications.

faqs.question: Do you replace all injectors or just failed ones?
faqs.answer: We follow a replace only what is needed approach. Testing identifies which injectors need service or replacement and which injectors are still in good condition, so you can avoid unnecessary full set replacement when the results support it.

faqs.question: What tests are included for common rail injectors?
faqs.answer: Common rail testing can include high pressure nozzle and control valve leak testing, injector start behavior, idle speed adjustment tuning, full load quantity, electric buzz testing, pilot injection quantity, idle quantity, emissions quantity, actuator resistance, and nozzle condition checks.

faqs.question: Why is fuel quality important for common rail injectors?
faqs.answer: Common rail injectors operate at very high pressure and have tighter internal tolerances than older diesel injectors. Poor fuel quality or contamination can damage internal components and lead to leak, quantity, or response problems.

faqs.question: Can the Bosch EPS205 test non Bosch injectors?
faqs.answer: Yes. The EPS205 is warranty approved for Bosch common rail injectors and can also test many Denso, Delphi, and Siemens common rail injectors.

detailSections.title: Testing Before Rebuilding
detailSections.text: Mechanical injector service begins with accurate testing. Our technicians check the spray pattern, nozzle chatter, opening pressure, and leak condition so the injector can be evaluated before any parts are replaced. This helps identify worn nozzles, weak springs, sealing issues, and poor atomization that can cause smoke, hard starting, rough idle, fuel knock, or uneven cylinder performance.

detailSections.title: Rebuild Decisions Based On Condition
detailSections.text: Unlike gasoline fuel injectors, many mechanical diesel injectors can be disassembled for a deeper internal inspection. We take the injector apart, clean and examine the internal components, then separate reusable parts from worn, repairable, or replaceable parts. The goal is to rebuild what makes sense while protecting the reliability of the fuel system.

image.alt: Mechanical diesel injector rebuilding and internal inspection at NW Fuel Injection Services

faqs.question: What mechanical injectors can you test and rebuild?

faqs.question: What is checked during mechanical injector testing?
faqs.answer: Testing includes spray pattern, nozzle chatter, opening pressure, and leak condition. Two spring injectors can also be checked for primary and secondary opening pressures.

faqs.question: Do you use OEM nozzles?

faqs.question: Should I test injectors before rebuilding them?

detailSections.text: Before injectors are placed in the ultrasonic cleaning bath, we run a pre test to measure flow rate, spray pattern, and general operation. This establishes a baseline so the injector can be compared after cleaning, rather than relying on guesswork.

image.alt: Gasoline fuel injector flow testing and spray pattern inspection before ultrasonic cleaning

items: Flow rate measured before cleaning
Spray pattern inspected before cleaning
General injector operation checked before service
Baseline results recorded for comparison
Problem injectors identified before additional work

detailSections.title: Ultrasonic Cleaning And Final Report
detailSections.text: Because gasoline injectors do not come apart for internal service, ultrasonic cleaning is used to reach internal areas that cannot be cleaned by hand. We pulse the injectors during cleaning to help flush internal components, then repeat the same tests after cleaning. Your injectors are returned with a written report, before and after results, and the necessary gaskets and seals for reinstallation.

Written before and after results supplied

faqs.question: What types of gasoline injectors do you clean?
faqs.answer: We test and clean top feed, side feed, and gasoline direct injection injectors using the ASNU Classic GDI cleaning machine.

faqs.question: What is included with gasoline injector cleaning?
faqs.answer: Service includes pre testing, ultrasonic cleaning, post testing, a written before and after report, and the necessary gaskets and seals for reinstallation.

faqs.question: What if cleaning does not fix my injectors?
faqs.answer: We operate a no fix, no pay policy. If ultrasonic cleaning cannot resolve the injector issue because of a shorted coil, physical damage, or another non cleanable failure, you do not pay for the cleaning service.

faqs.question: How much does gasoline injector cleaning cost?
faqs.answer: Top feed injectors are $39, side feed injectors are $49, and GDI injectors are $59. Additional gaskets or seals may cost $5 to $10 if needed.

faqs.question: How can I keep gasoline injectors cleaner for longer?
faqs.answer: Use good quality gasoline, keep up with regular vehicle maintenance, and follow the manufacturer's service recommendations, especially on modern gasoline direct injection systems.
